newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrilla leader captured, says source.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrilla leader captured, says source.

text.p: The Mexican military has captured a top commander of the guerrilla group, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a military sourse said on Wednesday.
The source said the commander, known as Hermenegildo, was captured during a gunbattle on Tuesday in this southwestern state of Guerrero.
Hermenegildo was the name used by the author of several communiques sent by the Marxist rebel group involved in at least two gunbattles with authorities since Saturday.
The source also said that a military general, Alfredo Oropeza Garnica, was wounded by two gunshots in the battle. He was taken to a military base.

The local military command said three soldiers and two gunmen were killed in Tuesday's incident, which took place in the hot, dusty peasant town of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of Acapulco. The gunmen, carrying AK-47 assault rifles, were later identified as EPR members.
Residents of the town said that a small military airplane had been hit by firing from the rebels and crashed, but that had not been confirmed.
The source, who declined to be identified, said Hermenegildo was being questioned at a military base.
Military spokesmen could not confirm whether the events took place.
The EPR first appeared in the state at the end of June 1996 calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government.

It launched a series of attacks last year, but had not attacked this year until Saturday, when rebels distributing propaganda opened fire when an army patrol came upon them on a remote road about 60 miles (100 km) east of the state capital Chilpancingo.
At least two soldiers and two rebels died in that battle.
